# JON PASCUAI — Portfolio

## 1. Project purpose

This repository contains the personal portfolio website of Jon Pascual.

The website represents the personal brand:

JON PASCUAI

The brand name is based on:

PASCUAL + AI

The website should communicate a professional identity focused on
software engineering, technology and Artificial Intelligence.

This is a personal professional portfolio, not a SaaS product or
generic developer template.

---

## 2. Personal information

Name:
Jon Pascual

Professional identity:
Software Developer & AI Engineer

Education:
Computer Engineering student at the University of Deusto.

Professional direction:
Artificial Intelligence, software engineering, technology and innovation.

Important:
Do not invent professional experience, qualifications, projects,
certifications or achievements that have not been provided by the user.

If information is missing, use a clear placeholder or ask the user
instead of inventing information.

---

## 3. Target audience

The primary audience is:

- Technology companies
- Consulting companies
- Technology professionals
- AI professionals
- Recruiters
- Potential employers

The website should communicate:

- Innovation
- Technology
- Professionalism
- Curiosity

The experience should make the visitor understand quickly:

1. Who Jon is.
2. What he does.
3. What he is interested in.
4. What he has built.
5. How to contact him.

---

## 4. Brand identity

The visual identity is:

- Minimalist
- Technical
- Professional
- Modern
- Clean
- Editorial
- Technology-oriented

Avoid making the website look like a generic AI landing page.

The design should feel like a carefully designed personal brand.

---

## 5. Brand colors

Use the official brand palette:

Black:
#111111

White:
#FFFFFF

Deep navy:
#102A43

Petrol blue:
#0B6E8E

The petrol blue should be used as the main accent color.

Do not introduce unrelated colors unless there is a clear accessibility
or functional reason.

When possible, use the existing brand colors consistently rather than
creating new shades arbitrarily.

---

## 6. Logo and naming

The primary brand name is:

JON PASCUAI

The logo concept visually separates:

JON + PASCU + AI

The brand must always be written correctly as:

JON PASCUAI

Do not rename the brand.

Do not replace the brand with generic alternatives such as:

- Jon AI
- Jon Pascual AI
- Pascual AI
- AI Developer Jon

unless explicitly requested by the user.

---

## 7. Typography

The brand identity references:

- Impact
- Garet

Use these fonts when legally and technically appropriate.

If they are not available for web use, select close alternatives.

Headings should have a strong, condensed and editorial appearance.

Body text should prioritize:

- readability
- clean typography
- good line height
- professional appearance

Do not use excessive font weights or excessive typography styles.

---

## 8. Visual language

Prefer:

- strong typography
- generous whitespace
- precise alignment
- editorial layouts
- thin borders
- subtle shadows
- technical details
- restrained use of color
- asymmetric compositions when appropriate
- elegant micro-interactions

Avoid:

- excessive gradients
- neon colors
- excessive glassmorphism
- excessive rounded cards
- excessive shadows
- generic stock imagery
- repetitive card grids
- excessive animations
- template-like layouts

The website should have visual personality without becoming visually noisy.

---

## 9. Technology stack

The project uses:

- React
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Tailwind CSS
- ESLint
- Lucide React
- Motion

Use TypeScript strictly.

Prefer reusable React components.

Prefer semantic HTML.

Prefer maintainable and simple architecture.

Do not add dependencies unless they provide meaningful value.

Before introducing a new dependency, consider whether the functionality
can be implemented cleanly with the existing stack.

---

## 10. Code quality

Write production-quality code.

Follow these principles:

- Keep components focused.
- Avoid unnecessarily large components.
- Avoid duplicated code.
- Use meaningful names.
- Use TypeScript types instead of `any`.
- Prefer reusable components.
- Keep data separate from presentation when appropriate.
- Use semantic HTML.
- Keep accessibility in mind.
- Avoid unnecessary state.
- Avoid unnecessary effects.
- Keep the architecture understandable.

Do not over-engineer simple functionality.

---

## 11. Responsive design

The website must work properly on:

- desktop
- laptop
- tablet
- mobile

Do not simply shrink the desktop layout.

Recompose sections when necessary for smaller screens.

Pay particular attention to:

- typography
- navigation
- spacing
- images
- project layouts
- buttons
- touch targets

No horizontal scrolling should appear on normal mobile devices.

---

## 12. Accessibility

Prioritize accessibility.

Use:

- semantic HTML
- accessible buttons
- accessible links
- appropriate heading hierarchy
- alt text for meaningful images
- sufficient color contrast
- keyboard-friendly interactions
- visible focus states

Do not use animation as the only way to communicate information.

Respect reduced-motion preferences where appropriate.

---

## 13. Animation philosophy

Animations should make the interface feel polished,
not distracting.

Prefer:

- fade
- translate
- subtle scale
- hover transitions
- scroll reveals
- smooth section transitions

Avoid:

- excessive parallax
- bouncing elements
- constant movement
- long animations
- animations that interfere with reading

Animations should support hierarchy and interaction.

---

## 14. Content rules

The portfolio should be primarily in English.

Spanish may be introduced later as a secondary language.

Do not invent content.

When writing copy:

- keep it concise
- professional
- technically credible
- natural
- confident without exaggeration

Avoid generic phrases such as:

"I am a passionate developer who loves coding."

Prefer specific information about:

- engineering
- Artificial Intelligence
- projects
- technologies
- learning
- innovation

---

## 15. Portfolio structure

The website will progressively contain sections such as:

- Hero
- About
- Skills
- Projects
- Education
- Experience
- AI / Technology interests
- References or inspiration
- Contact

Do not implement all sections at once.

Build the website incrementally and verify each section before
moving to the next one.

---

## 16. Project presentation

Projects are one of the most important parts of the portfolio.

Projects should communicate:

- What was built.
- What problem it solves.
- Technologies used.
- Jon's contribution.
- Relevant technical decisions.
- GitHub repository when available.
- Live demo when available.

Do not make projects look like simple generic cards.

Prefer a case-study-oriented presentation.

---

## 17. UX principles

A recruiter should understand the website within a few seconds.

The interface should make it easy to:

- understand who Jon is
- see his technical focus
- explore projects
- access GitHub
- contact him
- navigate between sections

Navigation should remain simple.

Do not add functionality just because it is technically possible.

Every interaction should have a purpose.

---

## 18. Development workflow

Work incrementally.

Before making major architectural changes:

1. Analyze the current code.
2. Explain the proposed change.
3. Identify affected components.
4. Implement the smallest clean solution.
5. Verify that the application still works.

Do not rewrite working code unnecessarily.

Do not modify unrelated files.

When implementing a new section, first inspect the existing design
system and reuse established components and patterns.

---

## 19. Git workflow

Keep commits small and meaningful.

Prefer conventional commit-style messages such as:

feat: add hero section
feat: add projects section
fix: improve mobile navigation
style: refine typography
refactor: simplify project cards
docs: update README

Do not commit generated dependencies or build artifacts.

Never commit secrets, API keys, passwords or private credentials.

---

## 20. Copilot behavior

Act as a senior frontend engineer and UI/UX designer working
alongside the developer.

Do not blindly implement requests.

If a requested solution would damage:

- accessibility
- maintainability
- performance
- responsiveness
- visual consistency
- security

explain the problem and propose a better alternative.

Before large changes, inspect the relevant existing code.

When there are multiple reasonable approaches, briefly explain
the trade-offs and recommend one.

Do not fabricate information about Jon.

Always preserve the JON PASCUAI brand identity.

---

## 21. Design priority

When making design decisions, prioritize in this order:

1. Usability
2. Accessibility
3. Visual hierarchy
4. Brand consistency
5. Responsiveness
6. Performance
7. Animation
8. Decorative effects

The website should look impressive because of its design quality,
not because of excessive visual effects.
